skill.name: aws-penetration-testing
skill.description: Guides authorized AWS security assessments across IAM, metadata services, S3, Lambda, EC2, containers, databases, and VPC environments.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized AWS penetration tests, from enumeration through attack-path analysis and remediation.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: Many Ruby backtick and ordinary documentation URL alerts are false positives caused by Markdown. Confirmed findings include metadata credential theft, privilege escalation, backdoors, secret retrieval, target-volume access, and defense evasion through CloudTrail suppression.

remediation.issue: The skill teaches metadata credential theft and reuse.
remediation.suggestion: Replace live credential retrieval with mock responses, synthetic secrets, and defensive IMDS validation steps.

remediation.issue: The skill provides CloudTrail deletion and GuardDuty evasion guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove defense-evasion commands and replace them with detection validation that preserves all audit controls.

remediation.issue: The skill includes backdoor, persistence, remote execution, and target-volume access workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Limit content to isolated labs, require explicit approvals, and emphasize read-only evidence and rollback.

remediation.issue: Authorization is stated but not enforced by the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require account allowlists, scope confirmation, least-privilege identities, stop conditions, and approval before state-changing steps.

content.user_title: Assess AWS Security with Authorized Test Workflows
content.value_statement: AWS attack paths span many services and permissions. This skill organizes authorized enumeration, exploitation validation, evidence collection, and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Enumerates AWS identities, policies, roles, buckets, compute resources, and service configurations.
Explains IAM permissions that can create privilege escalation paths.
Documents EC2, container, and Lambda metadata credential access techniques.
Covers S3, Lambda, SSM, EBS, Secrets Manager, KMS, RDS, DynamoDB, and EKS assessment workflows.
Maps VPC resources and potential lateral movement paths.
Provides authorization, scoping, documentation, cleanup, and security checklist guidance.
limitations: It does not verify authorization or enforce assessment scope.
Many commands can change resources, expose secrets, trigger alerts, or disrupt logging.
Examples use placeholders and require careful adaptation to an isolated test environment.
It does not provide automated evidence capture, rollback, or complete service coverage.

use_cases.title: Validate a Cloud Security Review
use_cases.description: Create a scoped checklist for read-only AWS enumeration and evidence collection.

use_cases.title: Analyze IAM Attack Paths
use_cases.description: Review authorized IAM policies for escalation paths and least-privilege fixes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Detection Exercises
use_cases.description: Translate approved AWS techniques into monitored lab scenarios and defensive validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Read-Only Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authorized AWS lab scope. Create a read-only enumeration checklist with required permissions, evidence, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Review IAM Escalation Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these authorized IAM policies. Identify escalation paths, affected principals, safe validation steps, and least-privilege remediations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Controlled SSRF Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an approved SSRF test using mock metadata responses. Define evidence, monitoring, cleanup, and controls that prevent real credential retrieval.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate Cross-Service Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Correlate these authorized IAM, Lambda, S3, EKS, RDS, and VPC findings. Prioritize attack paths, detection gaps, and defensive fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a read-only assessment plan for an approved development account.
output_examples.output: Scope: development account only. Sequence: identity, IAM, logging, storage, compute, and networking. Record timestamps, request identifiers, findings, and stop conditions.

output_examples.input: Review a role that can pass another role and launch EC2 instances.
output_examples.output: High-risk path: the principal may launch compute with the passed role. Restrict PassRole resources, constrain launch actions, and alert on unusual combinations.

output_examples.input: Summarize remediation for a metadata credential exposure.
output_examples.output: Require IMDSv2, limit hop count, block untrusted proxy destinations, reduce instance-role permissions, rotate exposed credentials, and review metadata access logs.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization, define exact accounts and resources, and stop when scope is uncertain.
Prefer read-only validation, isolated labs, least-privilege test identities, and synthetic secrets.
Capture evidence, monitor detections, restore changed resources, and document cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not retrieve real credentials or secrets when mock evidence can validate the finding.
Do not disable CloudTrail, GuardDuty, or other controls during marketplace-driven workflows.
Do not create persistence, alter production identities, or mount target volumes without explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it only with written permission, defined scope, approved timing, and accountable oversight.

faq.question: Can it run an AWS assessment automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and workflows, but it does not enforce scope, approvals, rollback, or evidence handling.

faq.question: Which AWS services are covered?
faq.answer: It covers IAM, EC2, S3, Lambda, SSM, EBS, ECS, EKS, ECR, RDS, DynamoDB, KMS, Secrets Manager, and VPC.

faq.question: Can I use it in production?
faq.answer: Use read-only checks first. Any state-changing test needs explicit approval, monitoring, backups, stop conditions, and a rollback plan.

faq.question: Does it include defensive guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a security checklist and can support remediation planning, although much of the source material is offensive.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use dedicated temporary test credentials with minimal permissions. Never place real secrets in prompts, reports, shell history, or shared logs.
